Explain the example for test and reset your practice app

blocks.text: A PWA needs tests for first visit, repeat visit, offline use and updates. Old workers and caches can hide mistakes during development.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.code:
Open Application tools on your own local project.
Check manifest errors and worker scope.
Load once online, then test offline navigation.
Change sw.js and inspect the waiting version.
For a clean test, unregister only your practice worker and clear only its app caches.
blocks.title: Test and reset your practice app

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: The first online load gives the worker a chance to install its offline files.
An update test checks both the waiting worker and existing pages, while a clean test starts without saved state.

blocks.text: These checks show whether the fallback, scope and update behaviour match your design.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: Do not clear unrelated site data. A clean local test and a real returning visit are different tests.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Test the offline page after one successful online visit.
